speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to pinpoint the cause, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms, especially given your history as a bodybuilder, alcohol use, and steroid use. Did the weakness start in the upper arm, the shoulder, or closer to your hand? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Metabolic_Panel, Lipid_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent lab results show normal readings, which is helpful. Given your significant weight loss and steroid use, have you noticed any visible atrophy (wasting) of the muscles in your right arm or shoulder?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sensation of "burning" and the progression of weakness combined with your steroid use and weight loss raises concern for a compressive neuropathy, likely cervical radiculopathy or brachial plexopathy. Can you tell me if the pain radiates from your neck down into your arm, or if it stays confined to the arm? REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI, Right_Upper_Extremity_Nerve_Conduction_Study.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of heavy smoking, significant weight loss, and anabolic steroid use raises concern for an underlying malignancy, such as Pancoast tumor or lymphoma, compressing the brachial plexus. Have you noticed any difficulty gripping objects or weakness spreading to your hand? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news; the absence of fever, vision changes, speech difficulties, or balance issues makes a central nervous system event like a stroke or meningitis highly unlikely. Your symptoms are now pointing strongly toward a peripheral issue, specifically involving the brachial plexus or cervical nerve roots. Given your significant weight loss, smoking history, and anabolic steroid use, we must rule out a malignancy such as a Pancoast tumor compressing the nerves. To confirm this, I need you to review the results of the Chest_X-Ray and Cervical_Spine_MRI images I requested earlier. Have you had a chance to see those results yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing compressive brachial plexopathy.
